verdicts.quote: All-or-nothing. A file that has any problem creates no user at all, and every problem found is reported.
one entry per row error, ordered by row then column, **all** errors listed ... Each error carries: `row`, `column` ..., `code`, `message` in words an admin can act on

Within the file, case-insensitively after trimming: the first occurrence is valid; every later occurrence gets `ROW_EMAIL_DUPLICATE_IN_FILE` ... Against existing accounts, including deactivated ones ...: `ROW_EMAIL_EXISTS`. ... Existing accounts are never changed.
`admin` or any role the import may not grant gives `ROW_ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED` (A-7). ... there is no input in any column by which an import creates an admin
The import page and the import endpoint are available to a signed-in user holding the admin role and to nobody else.
verdicts.missing: Whether the import permission is distinct from the single-user create permission (a non-admin who may create one user is not stated either way).

verdicts.quote: Header row required. Recognized columns: `email` (required), `name` (required), `role` (optional). ... Unknown column ...: 422 `HEADER_UNKNOWN_COLUMN` ... Missing required column: 422 `HEADER_MISSING_COLUMN`.
fields may be double-quoted, a quoted field may hold commas, doubled quotes and line breaks; `\n` and `\r\n` both end a record. ... BOM ignored.
an import sends the same message to each created user, **after** the atomic commit of R-6 and never for a rejected or failed import.
larger than 1,048,576 bytes: 413 `FILE_TOO_LARGE` ... More than 1,000 data records: 422 `TOO_MANY_ROWS` stating the limit and the count found; no row is validated.
zero bytes: 422 `FILE_EMPTY`. ... Header only, or no non-empty record after it: 422 `NO_DATA_ROWS`. ... a single-row file creates one.
The same file submitted twice (double click, retry after a timeout): the first creates; the second finds every email existing and is rejected with `ROW_EMAIL_EXISTS` for each row, creating nothing.
The import is synchronous: one request carries the file and returns the final result. No background job.
an import sends the same message to each created user, **after** the atomic commit ... At most one message per created user per import.
verdicts.missing: Whether up to 1,000 messages go out at once or are paced/throttled, and at what rate.

verdicts.quote: the same initial state, credential state and timestamps as a single-create user (A-3) ... How a created user first signs in is whatever single-create does (A-3).
verdicts.missing: The actual initial state (active or pending) and sign-in mechanism; deferred to unknown single-create behaviour (G-1).

verdicts.quote: The file and the parsed rows exist only in the memory of the request. They are not written to disk, caches, error trackers, request logs or the audit record.

Semicolon-separated files (some locales) are not supported: they fail as `HEADER_MISSING_COLUMN` and the help text names the comma separator. ... Dimension "fields a row holds" lists `email`, `name`, `role`.
Every submission that passes R-1 writes one audit record: import id, acting admin id, UTC timestamp, outcome ..., data-row count when known, created count, error count per code.
Not cancellable in this version. ... Makes retry after correction safe and removes the half-imported state.
Numeric target for response time at 1,000 rows: **unresolved** ... a status "Importing N bytes..." appears without a made-up progress percentage
verdicts.missing: A numeric time bound for a maximum-size file.

verdicts.quote: Existing users are never created twice, modified, deactivated or deleted by an import. The single-user create, sign-in, role management, user list and any export behave as before.
No CSV result export exists in this version, so formula-injection is `n/a`; if one is added, cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` must be neutralized. ... name ... 1 to 100 characters
